#define XI3CPSX_DYNAMIC_ADDR_PARITY_SHIFT   7U

Defines the odd-parity bit position in an encoded dynamic address.

Bit position of the odd-parity bit within the 8-bit encoded I3C dynamic address.

The encoded dynamic address is an 8-bit field: bit[7] is the odd parity of the 7-bit dynamic address (bits[6:0]), that is, parity = ~XOR(addr[6:0]). This matches the MIPI I3C bus format and the DEV_ADDR_TABLE_LOC*.DEV_DYNAMIC_ADDR[23:16] field layout, where bit[23] (= bit[7] of the 8-bit field) is the parity bit.

s32 XI3cPsx_BusInit ( XI3cPsx *  InstancePtr)

Initializes the I3C bus.

It configures the device address table, then resets and assigns the dynamic address to the slave devices.

Parameters
[in,out]InstancePtrPointer to the XI3cPsx instance.
Returns
  • XST_SUCCESS if successful.
  • XST_FAILURE otherwise.
Note
SCL timing must be programmed before calling this function. Call XI3cPsx_SetSClk() or XI3cPsx_SetSClkRate() first so that the RSTDAA and ENTDAA bus transactions issued here run at the intended clock rate. XI3cPsx_CfgInitialize() handles this sequence automatically; callers invoking XI3cPsx_BusInit() directly are responsible for calling XI3cPsx_SetSClk() first.

References XI3cPsx_Config::BaseAddress, CmdInfo::Cmd, XI3cPsx::Config, XI3cPsx_Config::DeviceCount, XI3cPsx::Error, I3C_CCC_ENTDAA, I3C_CCC_RSTDAA, CmdInfo::RxLen, CmdInfo::SlaveAddr, XI3C_DynaAddrList, XI3CPSX_DEVICE_ADDR, XI3CPSX_DEVICE_ADDR_DYNAMIC_ADDR_SHIFT, XI3CPSX_DEVICE_ADDR_DYNAMIC_ADDR_VALID_MASK, XI3CPSX_DEVICE_ADDR_SELF_DYNAMIC_ADDR, XI3CPSX_RESPONSE_ERR_ADDR_NACK, XI3CPSX_RESPONSE_ERR_IBA_NACK, XI3cPsx_SendAddrAssignCmd(), XI3cPsx_SendTransferCmd(), and XI3cPsx_WriteReg.

Referenced by XI3cPsx_CfgInitialize().

s32 XI3cPsx_CfgInitialize ( XI3cPsx *  InstancePtr,
XI3cPsx_Config *  ConfigPtr,
u32  EffectiveAddr 
)

Initializes an XI3cPsx instance so the driver is ready to use.

Parameters
[in,out]InstancePtrPointer to the XI3cPsx instance.
[in]ConfigPtrReference to a structure containing information about a specific I3C device. This function initializes an InstancePtr object for a specific device specified by the contents of Config.
[in]EffectiveAddrThe device base address in the virtual memory address space. The caller is responsible for keeping the address mapping from EffectiveAddr to the device physical base address unchanged once this function is invoked. Unexpected errors may occur if the address mapping changes after this function is called. If address translation is not used, use ConfigPtr->BaseAddress for this parameter, passing the physical address instead.
Returns
  • XST_SUCCESS if successful.

void XI3cPsx_MasterInterruptHandler ( XI3cPsx *  InstancePtr)

Handles interrupts in master mode.

It does the protocol handling for the interrupt-driven transfers.

If the Master is receiving data then the data is read from the FIFO and the Master has to request for more data (if there is more data to receive). If all the data has been received then a completion event is signalled to the upper layer by calling the callback handler. It is an error if the amount of received data is more than expected.

Parameters
[in,out]InstancePtrPointer to the XI3cPsx instance.

void XI3cPsx_RecoverFromError ( XI3cPsx *  InstancePtr)

Brings the controller back to a usable state after a transfer error.

An error response such as a receive buffer overflow leaves the core halted, and it stays halted until RESUME is written. The FIFOs are cleared after that because a transfer aborted part way through can leave untransmitted data behind in the TX FIFO.

This does not restore a target that has latched an error into its CCC_DEVICE_STATUS; that register is read only and needs the controller to read it with GETSTATUS.

Parameters
[in,out]InstancePtrPointer to the XI3cPsx instance.
Note
RESUME must be written before the FIFOs are reset. Resetting the FIFOs of a halted core leaves it halted.

References XI3cPsx::IsReady, XI3cPsx::RecvByteCount, XI3cPsx::SendByteCount, and XI3cPsx_ResetFifos().

void XI3cPsx_Reset ( XI3cPsx *  InstancePtr)

Resets the I3C controller.

Reset must only be called after the driver has been initialized. The configuration of the device after reset is the same as its configuration after initialization. Any data transfer that is in progress is aborted.

The upper layer software is responsible for re-configuring (if necessary) and reenabling interrupts for the I3C device after the reset.

void XI3cPsx_SlaveInterruptHandler ( XI3cPsx *  InstancePtr)

Handles interrupts in slave mode.

It does the protocol handling for the interrupt-driven transfers.

Completion events and errors are signaled to upper layer for proper handling.

The interrupts that are handled are:

  • DATA If the instance is sending, it means that the master wants to read more data from us. Send more data, and check whether we are done with this send.

    If the instance is receiving, it means that the master has written more data to us. Receive more data, and check whether we are done with with this receive.

  • COMP This marks that stop sequence has been sent from the master, transfer is about to terminate. However, for receiving, the master may have written us some data, so receive that first.

    It is an error if the amount of transferred data is less than expected.

  • NAK This marks that master does not want our data. It is for send only.
  • Other interrupts These interrupts are marked as error.
Parameters
[in,out]InstancePtrPointer to the XI3cPsx instance.
